title: Where we are headed
body:
Welcome to the first day. For the next 30 days we are going to hide the Beatitudes in our hearts, one line at a time, until we can say the whole thing from memory.

Jesus saw the crowds, went up on the mountainside, and sat down to teach. The first thing out of His mouth was not a rule. It was a list of who is blessed. And almost every person on the list is someone the world would overlook. The poor in spirit. The mourning. The meek. This is the upside down kingdom, and we are going to carry it in our hearts.

Today, just read the whole passage a few times. Do not try to memorize anything yet. Let it wash over you. Tomorrow we start with the very first line.
practice: Read Matthew 5:1-12 out loud three times. That is all today.

title: Poor in spirit
body:
Here is our first line to learn: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

Poor in spirit does not mean poor in money. It means knowing you are empty without God. It is the person who has stopped pretending they have it all together and finally admits they need Him. That is where the kingdom begins. Not with the strong and self-made, but with the ones honest enough to say I cannot do this on my own.

God is not looking for people who are impressive. He is looking for people who are open. Emptiness is not a problem to Him. It is the doorway.
practice: Say Matthew 5:3 ten times today. Once when you wake up, and again every time you get a drink of water.

title: Poor in spirit, in real life
body:
Being poor in spirit shows up in ordinary moments. It is the prayer you whisper when you do not know what to do. It is asking for help instead of white knuckling it. It is the relief of stopping the performance.

The world tells us to be self-sufficient, to never let them see you struggle. Jesus says the ones who admit their need are the ones who get the whole kingdom. What a trade.

Where in your life are you still pretending to be fine? That is exactly where He wants to meet you.
practice: Cover part of the verse in the practice game and fill in the rest from memory. Then say it once more before bed.

title: Lock in the first line
body:
Today we make the first line stick. You should be able to say Matthew 5:3 without looking now, or close to it.

Here is a memory trick that works: attach the words to a picture. Picture an empty cupped hand held open, waiting to be filled. Poor in spirit, hands open, kingdom poured in. Your brain remembers pictures long after it forgets words.

One down. Seven to go. You are already building something.
practice: Say Matthew 5:3 from memory five times. Try writing it on a sticky note and putting it on your mirror.

title: Those who mourn
body:
The second line: Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted.

This one is tender. Jesus does not skip over grief or rush us past it. He blesses it. He says the ones who mourn are not forgotten, they are comforted. There is a kind of sorrow that softens us instead of hardening us, that turns us toward God instead of away.

We mourn our own sin. We mourn a broken world. We mourn people we have lost. And into all of it, God does not say get over it. He says I will comfort you.
practice: Add Matthew 5:4 to your practice. Then say verses 3 and 4 back to back.

title: Comfort that actually comes
body:
The promise is not that we will avoid grief. It is that grief will not get the last word. Comfort comes. Sometimes through Scripture, sometimes through a friend who shows up, sometimes through a peace you cannot explain.

If you are in a hard season right now, this verse is for you. You are not being punished. You are being carried. The comfort is on its way, and often it comes in the middle of the mourning, not only after.

Do not hide your tears from God. He counts them.
practice: Say verses 3 and 4 together from memory. Notice how they start the same way. That pattern is your friend.

title: Lock in the second line
body:
Two lines down. Every Beatitude starts with Blessed are, and that repetition is doing the heavy lifting for your memory. Lean on it.

Try saying both verses out loud in the car today. Something about saying it while you drive locks it in. No one is watching. Just you and the words.

You are one quarter of the way to the kingdom list living in your heart.
practice: Say Matthew 5:3 and 5:4 from memory three times. Play the hide game and push the difficulty up one notch.

title: The meek
body:
Line three: Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth.

Meek is one of the most misunderstood words in the Bible. It does not mean weak. It means strength under control. Think of a powerful horse that has learned to be gentle. The meek are not pushovers. They are people who could push back and choose not to, because they trust God to handle it.

The world says grab everything you can. Jesus says the gentle ones inherit it all in the end. You do not have to claw your way to the top. You can trust the One who owns the earth.
practice: Add Matthew 5:5. Say verses 3, 4, and 5 in order.

title: Strength that stays gentle
body:
Meekness is the mom who could yell but kneels down instead. It is the person in the meeting who could win the argument but keeps the peace. It is choosing gentleness when you have every right to come out swinging.

That kind of restraint is not weakness. It takes more strength than lashing out ever did. And Jesus says it is the meek, not the loud, who inherit the earth.

Who in your life needs your gentleness today, especially when they do not deserve it?
practice: Say verses 3 through 5 from memory. Use the hide game to check yourself.

title: Lock in the third line
body:
Three down. You now have poor in spirit, mourn, meek. Notice they build on each other. First you know your need, then you grieve what is broken, then you hold your strength gently. There is an order to becoming like Jesus.

This is a good day to write all three on a card and tape it somewhere you look every day. The fridge. The bathroom mirror. Your car dashboard.
practice: Say Matthew 5:3-5 from memory five times. Print a card from the resources and put it somewhere you will see it.

title: Hunger and thirst
body:
Line four: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be filled.

We are at the center of the list now. Hunger and thirst are not casual wants. They are needs you feel in your body. Jesus is describing people who want to be right with God and want to see the world made right the way a starving person wants food.

And the promise is stunning. They will be filled. God never starves a hungry heart. If you actually want more of Him, that desire itself is a gift, and He will not leave it empty.
practice: Add Matthew 5:6. Say verses 3 through 6 in order.

title: What you hunger for
body:
We hunger for a lot of things that never fill us. More stuff, more approval, more scrolling. We keep eating and stay hungry. Jesus points to the one hunger that actually gets satisfied, wanting to be right with God.

Here is the good news hiding in this verse. You do not have to manufacture righteousness. You just have to want it. The wanting is the doorway. He does the filling.

What have you been trying to fill up on lately that has left you empty?
practice: Say verses 3 through 6 from memory. You are at the halfway point of the eight.

title: Lock in the fourth line
body:
Four down, four to go. You are halfway. Take a second to be proud of that. Two weeks ago these were words on a page, and now they live in you.

Today, try reciting all four without looking at all. If you get stuck, that is fine. Getting stuck and pushing through is exactly how memory gets strong. The struggle is the workout.
practice: Say Matthew 5:3-6 from memory. Then try saying it to another person out loud, even a kid.

title: The merciful
body:
Line five: Blessed are the merciful, for they will be shown mercy.

Mercy is love with its sleeves rolled up. It is not just feeling bad for someone, it is doing something about it. Forgiving the debt. Making the meal. Giving the second chance you were not obligated to give.

And notice the return. The merciful will be shown mercy. This is not earning God's mercy, we already have it. It is that mercy given has a way of flowing back to you. The hand that gives is the hand that receives.
practice: Add Matthew 5:7. Say verses 3 through 7 in order.

title: Mercy in action
body:
Mercy usually costs something. Time, money, pride, the right to be right. That is what makes it mercy and not just being nice. Jesus was merciful all the way to a cross.

We find it easy to want mercy for ourselves and justice for everyone else. This verse flips that. Be the one who gives the grace you hope to receive.

Is there someone you have been holding a debt against? Today might be the day to let it go.
practice: Say verses 3 through 7 from memory. Show one act of mercy to someone today, even a small one.

title: Lock in the fifth line
body:
Five down. Look how far you have come. Poor in spirit, mourn, meek, hunger and thirst, merciful. You are carrying more than half of the Beatitudes in your heart now.

A good test today. Say them while you are doing something else, folding laundry, walking, driving. If you can say them with your hands busy, they are becoming part of you, not just something you recite.
practice: Say Matthew 5:3-7 from memory while doing a chore. Push the hide game up a level.

title: The pure in heart
body:
Line six: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.

Pure in heart means undivided. It is a heart that is not split between God and a hundred other loyalties. Not perfect, but honest. No hidden rooms, no secret self. What you see is what is really there.

And the promise is the greatest one yet. They will see God. Purity is not about being good enough to earn a look at Him. It is that a clean window lets the light through. When our hearts are undivided, we finally see Him clearly.
practice: Add Matthew 5:8. Say verses 3 through 8 in order.

title: An undivided heart
body:
A divided heart is exhausting. Trying to serve God and also protect an image, chase approval, and keep a secret all at once will wear you out. Jesus offers something simpler. One heart, pointed one way.

Purity of heart is not about never messing up. It is about not hiding when you do. It is bringing the whole self into the light, even the parts you are ashamed of. That is where you see God most clearly, in the honesty.

Is there a corner of your heart you have kept in the dark? He is gentle. Bring it to Him.
practice: Say verses 3 through 8 from memory. Sit quiet for one minute and ask God to make your heart undivided.

title: Lock in the sixth line
body:
Six down. Only two more Beatitudes to learn. You are so close to having the whole list.

Here is a fun one for today. If you have kids around, teach them verse 8. Kids memorize fast, and teaching someone else is the best way to cement it in your own mind. Make it a little game at dinner.
practice: Say Matthew 5:3-8 from memory. Teach one verse to someone younger than you.

title: The peacemakers
body:
Line seven: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.

Notice it says peacemakers, not peacekeepers. Keeping the peace often means avoiding, staying quiet, letting things slide. Making peace is active. It steps into the mess and works to reconcile. It costs something.

And look at the reward. They will be called children of God. When you make peace, you look like your Father, because that is exactly what He did for us through Jesus. Peacemaking is the family resemblance.
practice: Add Matthew 5:9. Say verses 3 through 9 in order.

title: Make peace, do not just keep it
body:
Peacemaking is hard because it usually means going first. Being the one to apologize, to reach out, to break the silence. It is easier to keep score. But Jesus blesses the ones who lay down the scorecard and build a bridge.

This does not mean pretending everything is fine. Real peace deals with the real thing. It is honest and kind at the same time.

Is there a relationship where you could go first this week?
practice: Say verses 3 through 9 from memory. Take one step toward peace with someone today.

title: Lock in the seventh line
body:
Seven down. One Beatitude left. You can almost say the whole thing.

You are at the level now where the hide game should be covering half the words and you can still fill them in. If that feels hard, that is normal. Keep going back to the ones that trip you up. Those sticky spots just need a few more reps.
practice: Say Matthew 5:3-9 from memory twice. Spend extra time on any line that trips you up.

title: The persecuted
body:
The eighth and final line: Blessed are those who are persecuted because of righteousness, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

This is the hard one. Jesus is honest that doing the right thing sometimes costs you. People may misunderstand you, push back, even turn on you. He does not promise the Christian life will be easy. He promises it will be worth it.

And look, the list ends where it began. Theirs is the kingdom of heaven. The very same reward as the poor in spirit. The circle closes. Blessing at the start, blessing at the end.
practice: Add Matthew 5:10. You now have all eight. Say verses 3 through 10 in order.

title: Blessed when it costs you
body:
Most of us will not face real persecution. But we all know the smaller version, being left out, laughed at, or judged for doing what is right. Jesus sees it, and He calls it blessed.

The reward is not someday only. It is theirs, present tense, the kingdom of heaven belongs to them right now. When standing for what is right costs you, you are not losing. You are in good company, and the kingdom is yours.

Have you ever paid a price for doing the right thing? Jesus saw it.
practice: Say verses 3 through 10 from memory. That is all eight Beatitudes. Sit with that for a second.

title: Lock in all eight
body:
You did it. All eight Beatitudes are in your heart. Today is not about learning a new line, it is about running the whole list until it flows.

Say them start to finish. Then again. Then again. Each time it gets a little smoother. The goal is not just to recall them but to be able to say them like you mean them, because you do.

Tomorrow we add the last piece Jesus said, the part where He turns and speaks straight to you.
practice: Say Matthew 5:3-10 from memory three times. Smooth out the rough spots.

title: When they say all kinds of evil
body:
After the eight, Jesus turns personal. He stops saying blessed are they and starts saying blessed are you. Verses 11 and 12: Blessed are you when people insult you, persecute you and falsely say all kinds of evil against you because of me. Rejoice and be glad, because great is your reward in heaven.

This is Jesus looking right at you. When it comes, and it may, His instruction is almost shocking. Rejoice. Be glad. Not because the pain is not real, but because you are in the long line of prophets who stood for God and the reward is huge.

Add these two verses to your recitation. Now you have the whole passage.
practice: Add Matthew 5:11-12. Say the entire passage, verses 3 through 12, from memory.

title: Put it all together
body:
You have every piece now. Today we make it one smooth thing instead of nine separate parts.

Here is a tip. Say it with your body. Some people walk while they recite. Some tap the rhythm. Some have made up a simple tune and sing it, and honestly that is the fastest way of all. If a song helps you, make one up and do not overthink it. Nobody has to hear it but you and God.

Run the whole passage a few times today. You are almost there.
practice: Say Matthew 5:3-12 from memory. Try making up a simple tune for it, or walking while you say it.

title: Say it without looking
body:
Today, close the book and say the whole thing. When you hit a wall, do not peek right away. Sit in it for a second and let your memory reach for it. That reaching is what makes it permanent.

Most of the words are hidden in the practice game now. If you can fill in eighty percent from memory, you are ready for the home stretch.

You have carried this passage for almost a month. It is becoming part of who you are.
practice: Play the hide game at the hardest level you can. Say the whole passage out loud twice.

title: Almost there
body:
One day before the finish. Today, say the entire passage to another person. Your spouse, your kid, a friend, whoever. Saying it out loud to a real face is different than saying it alone, and it will show you how solid it really is.

Do not worry about being perfect. Worry about meaning it. These are not just words you memorized. This is the heart of Jesus, and it is in you now.

Tomorrow is the celebration, and your challenge to share it.
practice: Recite Matthew 5:3-12 to one other person, out loud, from memory.

title: You hid it in your heart
body:
Thirty days ago these were words on a page. Today they live in you. That is a real thing, and it does not go away. You have hidden the Beatitudes in your heart, and no one can take them.

Here is the final challenge, and it is a fun one. Record yourself saying the whole passage from memory. Just your phone, no need to be polished. Then share it. Post it on your dashboard here, and put it on Facebook or Instagram with the hashtag HideItInYourHeart. Your recording might be the nudge that gets someone else to start.

Then grab your certificate. You earned every word of it. I am so proud of you.
practice: Record yourself saying Matthew 5:3-12 from memory. Share it with #HideItInYourHeart, then open your certificate.
